item.title: Ronaldo’s 2008 Ballon d’Or named best of all time in fan vote
item.description: By Efe Onodjae Cristiano Ronaldo’s 2008 Ballon d’Or-winning campaign has been voted the best in the history of the prestigious individual football award in a public poll organised to celebrate its 70th anniversary. The result was posted by football transfer journalist, Fabrizio Romano, in a Facebook post monitored by Vanguard. Ronaldo’s 2008 triumph topped the Ballon d’Or of All Time (BOAT) ranking, ahead of Lionel Messi’s 2012 edition, while the Portuguese forward’s 2017 campaign came third. Messi’s 2023 season occupied the fourth position, followed by Ronaldo’s 2016 campaign in fifth place. The ranking featured 32 editions of the award won by 10 football legends, with supporters voting for the individual campaigns they considered the greatest. Other editions featuring prominently in the top 10 included Ronaldo’s 2014 and 2013 victories, as well as Messi’s 2015, 2011 and 2009 campaigns. Brazilian legend Ronaldo Nazário’s 2002 triumph was ranked 13th, while Johan Cruyff’s 1974 victory came 17th. Michel Platini’s 1984 campaign occupied the 18th position, ahead of Franz Beckenbauer’s 1976 edition. Ronaldo won his first Ballon d’Or in 2008 while playing for Manchester United, following an outstanding season in which he scored 42 goals in all competitions and helped the English club win the Premier League and UEFA Champions League. The Portuguese forward subsequently won the award four more times, in 2013, 2014, 2016 and 2017, taking his career tally to five. Messi, meanwhile, holds the record for the most Ballon d’Or wins, with eight, including his 2023 triumph following Argentina’s victory at the 2022 FIFA World Cup. The BOAT ranking recognises individual Ballon d’Or-winning campaigns rather than awarding a new official Ballon d’Or or determining which player has enjoyed the greatest career. The result is also separate from the annual Ballon d’Or award, which is decided through a jury of specialist journalists. The poll has renewed debate among football supporters over the achievements of Ronaldo and Messi, whose rivalry has dominated discussions about the world’s best player for more than a decade. item.title: Tinubu departs Abuja for Makkah to pray for Nigeria
item.description: President Bola Tinubu will depart Abuja on Thursday for Makkah, Saudi Arabia, to perform Umrah, an Islamic pilgrimage involving prayers and other religious rites. According to a statement issued on Wednesday by his Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, the visit will provide the President an opportunity for spiritual reflection and prayers for Nigeria’s peace, unity, stability and continued progress. While in Makkah, Tinubu is expected to perform the religious rites associated with Umrah and seek Allah’s guidance and blessings for Nigeria and its people. Before departing Abuja, the President will commission equipment acquired by the Nigerian Air Force at the Presidential Wing of the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport. Tinubu is expected to return to Nigeria next week after completing the spiritual exercise. The statement was dated October 28, 2026. item.title: Djokovic wins Basel opener to boost ATP Finals bid
item.description: Novak Djokovic dug deep to overcome Ugo Humbert in three sets in his opening match in Basel on Wednesday, keeping his bid to qualify for the season-ending ATP Finals on course. The 39-year-old Djokovic dropped the first set but recovered to beat the French left-hander 4-6, 6-3, 6-4 on his first appearance in Basel since 2011. Djokovic strengthened his chances of a record 19th qualification for the ATP Finals by winning the China Open in Beijing earlier this month, the 102nd title of his career. That was followed by an early exit at the Shanghai Masters, with the 24-time Grand Slam champion accepting a wild card into the Swiss event after slipping to 11th in the Race to Turin standings. Djokovic is a seven-time winner of the ATP Finals, but he did not compete at either of the past two editions because of injury. Only the top eight players qualify for the November 15-22 showpiece, although Jannik Sinner has already pulled out due to a knee problem. Fourth seed Djokovic takes on Germany’s Jan-Lennard Struff in the next round in Basel. He holds an 8-0 record against Struff. item.title: 2027 budget to be ready before end of December – FG
item.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — THE MINISTER of State for Budget, Dr Doris Uzoka-Anite, on Wednesday assured that the 2027 budget will be ready for presentation before the end of 2026 to allow for legislative consideration ahead of the new fiscal year. The Minister disclosed while fielding questions from State House correspondents at the end of the Federal Executive Council, FEC, meeting presided over by President Bola Tinubu at the Presidential Villa, Abuja. “We are working on the 2027 budget, and our intention is to present it before the end of the year,” Uzoka-Anite said. The planned timeline is expected to give the National Assembly an opportunity to scrutinise the proposed estimates and deliberate on the government’s revenue projections and expenditure priorities before the commencement of the 2027 fiscal year. The annual budget serves as the Federal Government’s principal fiscal policy instrument, setting out its spending priorities, revenue expectations and economic objectives for the year. The minister also announced that the council approved the revised 2026 national policy on food and nutrition in Nigeria and the National Nutrition Bill 2026. She said the documents were developed through collaboration among the office of the vice-president, the ministries of budget and economic planning, agriculture, livestock, education and health, as well as the private sector, the national assembly, and development partners. According to the minister, the documents provide a framework for coordinating and implementing food and nutrition programmes nationwide, while promoting sustainable funding and accountability. She said the measures are aimed at improving the health and wellbeing of Nigerians by reducing childhood stunting, adding that the nutrition bill, an executive bill, would be forwarded to the national assembly for consideration. item.title: 2027: PDP dismisses alleged election postponement plot
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has dismissed allegations of a plot to pressure the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to postpone the January 16, 2027 presidential election, insisting that the polls will hold peacefully. The party said it was unaware of any move to alter the election timetable, warning that reports circulating on social media could undermine public confidence in the electoral process and threaten national stability. PDP National Publicity Secretary, Jungudo Haruna Mohammed, stated this in his response to Vanguard’s inquiry on Wednesday, expressing confidence that President Bola Tinubu, the All Progressives Congress (APC) and INEC would adhere to the established electoral timetable. “We have seen some of the stories circulating on social media, but I do not believe them, and the PDP does not believe there is any plan whatsoever to alter the election timetable,” Jungudo said. He said the APC-led government and INEC were committed to conducting the elections in accordance with the Electoral Act and the commission’s published schedule of activities. Jungudo alleged that those spreading the reports were attempting to create confusion because they had realised they would make little impact in the elections. “Some people have clearly realised that they will not make any impact in the elections. What they have decided to do, therefore, is create confusion and undermine confidence in the process by sowing doubts in the minds of Nigerians,” he said. Warning that the consequences could extend beyond partisan politics, Jungudo said any threat to the credibility of the electoral process could affect the country as a whole. “Unfortunately, what they fail to understand is that this will not affect the APC or President Tinubu alone. It will affect Nigeria as a country,” he warned. He urged politicians to moderate their public statements and promote peace, confidence in the electoral process and trust in INEC’s impartiality. Jungudo also challenged opposition parties seeking to defeat the APC to unite and build a formidable political force. “I can assure you that the 2027 elections will hold, and they will hold peacefully, without any crisis, by the special grace of God,” he said. item.title: Niger State Assembly Commends Army For Foiling Attack By Bandits
item.description: ‎ ‎The Niger State House of Assembly has commended troops of the Nigerian Army for repelling a major attack by bandits on communities in Rafi Local Government Area of the state, which left one soldier dead and three others injured. ‎ ‎The House also called for the establishment of additional military bases in vulnerable communities to strengthen security, prevent bandits from regrouping, and improve rapid response to distress calls. ‎ ‎The commendation followed a motion moved by the member representing Rafi Constituency, Zubairu Zanna, during plenary on Tuesday. ‎ ‎The lawmaker praised the troops for their courage, professionalism and gallantry in confronting the armed men, saying their intervention prevented what could have resulted in a massacre of innocent residents. Niger State is in North-Central Nigeria ‎ About two weeks ago, more than 100 suspected bandits reportedly invaded communities along the Zungeru-Tegina Road but were met with stiff resistance from the Army, which successfully repelled the attack. ‎ ‎Although one soldier reportedly died from gunshot injuries while three others sustained injuries, several bandits were neutralised during the encounter, and motorcycles were recovered. ‎ ‎Zanna urged the Nigerian Army and other security agencies to sustain their operations and strengthen their presence in the affected communities to prevent further attacks. ‎ ‎He stressed the strategic and economic importance of the communities, noting that the establishment of a Forward Operating Base (FOB) would help prevent criminal groups from regrouping and launching fresh attacks. ‎ ‎According to him, the absence of military bases and strategically positioned security formations along identified vulnerable corridors could limit the ability of security personnel to respond swiftly to distress calls. ‎ ‎The lawmaker further observed that difficult terrain, extensive forests and inadequately secured rural routes in parts of the state, particularly Rafi Local Government Area, provided opportunities for criminal groups to infiltrate communities, establish camps and hideouts, and launch attacks on innocent residents. ‎ ‎He therefore called on the Niger State Government to urgently engage the Federal Government on the need to establish additional military bases and strengthen security deployments in vulnerable communities, particularly along routes frequently used by bandits. ‎ ‎The Speaker of the House, Abdulmalik Sarkindaji, who presided over the plenary, called for a minute of silence in honour of the fallen soldier and offered prayers for the speedy recovery of those receiving medical treatment. item.title: 92-year-old US judge handling Maduro case dies
item.description: Alvin Hellerstein, the US judge overseeing the case against deposed Venezuelan president Nicolas Maduro, has died aged 92, an official confirmed Wednesday. As one of the oldest US federal judges, questions had been raised about whether he was the right justice to preside over what could be a prolonged trial for Maduro on drug trafficking charges. Hellerstein’s lengthy career included overseeing the civil cases arising from Al-Qaeda’s September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks on New York and Washington, often rejecting deals he saw as unfair to complainants. His death was confirmed to AFP by an official at the United States District Court, Southern District of New York, where he presided. Hellerstein also tangled with Donald Trump, rejecting a request by the US president to have his New York hush money case moved to federal court. Last year, he blocked the Trump administration from deporting alleged Venezuelan gang members without a court hearing. In a noteworthy 2015 ruling, Hellerstein ordered the US government to release a trove of photos depicting abuse of detainees in Iraq and Afghanistan. He also presided over a trial last year in which a jury found French banking giant BNP Paribas’s work in Sudan had helped prop up the regime of former ruler Omar al-Bashir, awarding $20.75 million in damages to three plaintiffs from Sudan. Hellerstein handled the sprawling drug trafficking case linked to Maduro for over a decade, which has already seen the conviction of Venezuela’s former intelligence chief, Hugo Armando Carvajal. Maduro was seized by US forces in January in a military raid on his compound in Venezuela. A graduate of Columbia University law school, Hellerstein served as a lawyer in the US Army from 1957 to 1960 before entering private practice. He was nominated by then president Bill Clinton in 1998 to be a district court judge for the Southern District of New York. item.title: 2027: Adebayo threatens protest over alleged plot to postpone election
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike The Adewole Adebayo-Bugaje Presidential Campaign Council has threatened legal action and mass protests against any attempt to pressure the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, into postponing the January 16, 2027 presidential election. The council said the election timetable was non-negotiable, warning that any attempt to alter it, including under the guise of public health concerns, would undermine the democratic process and Nigerians’ right to choose their leaders. Speaking to Vanguard in Abuja on Wednesday, the campaign council’s Chief Media and Communications Adviser, Comrade Mark Adebayo, alleged a plot to summon INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, to the Presidential Villa to alter the election timetable. “We strongly condemn any covert or overt attempts to pressure INEC into altering the sacrosanct January 16, 2027, election timetable,” Adebayo said. He accused the Tinubu administration of preparing to manipulate the electoral process, citing what he described as its unpopularity. “We are aware that because of the unprecedented unpopularity of the Tinubu administration and the fact that Nigerians have totally rejected them, they have many rigging cards under their table to play,” he said. Adebayo also warned against using the reported Ebola outbreak as a pretext to delay the election, saying the campaign council would resist any such move through legal means and mass action. “Using public health concerns or engineered crises as political tools to evade an imminent electoral verdict will be fiercely resisted by all legal means, including mass actions,” he said. He urged INEC to remain neutral and reject any alleged pressure from the Presidency, insisting that the election timetable must be maintained. Adebayo said the campaign’s presidential candidate, Prince Adewole Adebayo, and his running mate, Dr Usman Bugaje, remained prepared for the polls, urging Nigerians to remain vigilant. “Nigerians are no fools, and any attempt to treat us that way stands to be stoutly resisted by the mass of Nigerians,” he added. item.title: Moonshot 2026: ‘Africans deserve better protection’ — Tech experts faults companies, govt over digital safety
item.description: By Efosa Taiwo Chioma Agwuegbo, executive director of TechHerNG, has called on technology companies to prioritise users’ safety, privacy and rights, warning that the rapid development of digital tools without adequate safeguards could expose women, children and persons with disabilities to greater risks. Agwuegbo spoke during the session titled “Designing Safer Digital Futures: Privacy, Protection and Rights in African Tech” at the Startup Stage of Moonshot 2026: Courage & Conviction. She criticised technology platforms for focusing on developing new products and features without adequately considering their potential harm to users. “Access and safety should be the floor,” she said, arguing that excluding people from safe participation in digital spaces undermines their agency. Agwuegbo cited the misuse of artificial intelligence to create non-consensual intimate images of women as an example of the dangers associated with emerging technologies. “For instance, Grok should never be able to nudify women,” she said, warning that harmful applications can emerge rapidly after new technologies become available. She noted that women and persons with disabilities were particularly vulnerable to the negative consequences of technological developments, stressing the need for platforms to consider potential abuses before launching new products. The TechHerNG director also raised concerns about the way technology companies treat African users compared with users in other parts of the world. According to her, people who experience online violence in some foreign jurisdictions may have access to stronger avenues for seeking redress, while African users often face limited options for holding platforms accountable. She said investment in user safety remained inadequate and called for technology companies to take greater responsibility for protecting the people who use their services. Agwuegbo also criticised African governments for failing to do enough to address digital safety concerns. “A lot of things we are suffering is because our govt is asleep,” she said. On protecting children online, she emphasised the importance of trust, context and open communication between parents and their children. Agwuegbo stressed that parents should create an environment where children feel comfortable discussing their online experiences rather than relying solely on restrictive measures. She also highlighted the role of regulators in ensuring that technology companies operate within appropriate safeguards, noting that oversight was necessary to prevent harm. The executive director further called on media organisations to report violence against women responsibly and help draw attention to the risks women face in digital spaces. Also speaking during the session, Modupe Adebimpe, head of operations and projects at ProsperityTech, highlighted the challenges of embedding safety measures into technology products, noting that doing so could be expensive. item.title: Pensioners blast NLC, FG over exclusion from ₦70,000 transport relief
item.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — The Nigeria Union of Pensioners (NUP) has condemned its exclusion from the newly approved ₦70,000 monthly transport allowance for workers, accusing the Federal Government and the leadership of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) of abandoning retired workers who are battling the same punishing cost of living. NUP National President, Comrade Godwin Abumisi, said the exclusion of pensioners from the six-month intervention — approved for public servants from November 2026 — was “unjust” and a painful reminder that those who spent their productive years in national service are being treated as an afterthought. “Pensioners also depend on public transportation to access hospitals, attend medical appointments, purchase food, and other essential items,” Abumisi said, stressing that many retirees live on inadequate pensions and have no other reliable income. The union questioned why the NLC, which negotiated for serving workers, did not push for corresponding relief for retired colleagues, calling the omission evidence of the “insensitivity of civil servants to the plight of their former colleagues, now retired, whom they will eventually join in retirement.” NUP argued that the welfare of workers and pensioners should not be treated as competing interests, warning that every serving employee will one day become a pensioner. The union also frowned at the government’s failure to pay the ₦25,000 monthly palliative promised under the Federal Government’s October 2, 2023 Memorandum of Understanding with the NLC and TUC. The agreement committed the government to pay ₦25,000 monthly for three months to 15 million households, including vulnerable pensioners — ₦75,000 per eligible beneficiary in total. More than three years later, NUP says many vulnerable pensioners have still not received the money. It demanded that the Federal Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction, led by Dr. Bernard M. Doro, explain what has stalled the payment and give a definite timeline. The union appealed directly to President Bola Tinubu to intervene urgently and extend the ₦70,000 transport allowance to eligible retirees, or provide an equivalent transport-support measure. NUP warned that it will pursue “all legitimate and lawful avenues” if the government fails to act, insisting that Nigerians who served the country faithfully must not be discarded in retirement. item.title: Odibola Properties, Mezie And The Danger Of Trial By Social Media: When Facts Must Prevail Over Allegations
item.description: In an era where social media allegations can threaten years of hard work, investment and reputation, the controversy involving Odibola Properties Limited and Chimezie Princewill Onwuka, popularly known as Mezie, raises serious questions about credibility, responsible advocacy and the importance of verifying facts before passing judgment. Odibola Properties Limited has positioned itself as a real estate development company committed to legitimate property acquisition, investment protection and integrity in business. Its Chief Executive Officer, Oshobukola Sunny Isaac, has publicly advocated against land grabbing in Rivers State, an effort recently recognised with the Anti-Land Grabbing Advocate of the Year 2026 Award at the Niger Delta Advancement Honours held on 24 October 2026. While such recognition is not a substitute for legal verification, it reflects the company’s publicly stated commitment to protecting property investors and promoting responsible real estate development. MEZIE: QUESTIONS ABOUT CREDIBILITY AND RESPONSIBLE ADVOCACY Chimezie Princewill Onwuka, popularly known as Mezie, has made allegations concerning Odibola Properties and its involvement in disputed land at Mbodo-Aluu, Rivers State. However, an important question deserves public attention: How thoroughly were the relevant legal documents examined before these allegations were presented to the public? There is also a reported disciplinary matter in his past that raises legitimate questions about accountability. If independently confirmed to concern the same individual, this history is relevant to assessing his public record, although it does not, by itself, establish that his present allegations are false. Nevertheless, anyone who assumes the responsibility of publicly questioning another person’s integrity must be willing to demonstrate accuracy, transparency and fairness in their own conduct. Public influence is not proof of credibility. Credibility must be earned through consistency, evidence and accountability. THE ODIBOLA LAND CONTROVERSY: WHAT HAS BEEN LEFT OUT? The allegation attributed to Mezie suggests that Odibola Properties acquired disputed family land through Fabulous Amaewhule without the involvement of the wider family. Odibola Properties has challenged that account. According to the company’s explanation, it did not purchase the land directly from Fabulous Amaewhule. Rather, it became involved through a Power of Attorney granted by an association of medical doctors following an out-of-court settlement with Fabulous Amaewhule, whom the company identifies as a judgment creditor in earlier proceedings involving the doctors. item.title: APC holds court-ordered rerun Primary in 11 Plateau wards
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS — The All Progressives Congress (APC) on Wednesday conducted a court-ordered rerun primary election in 11 wards of Jos South/Jos East Federal Constituency of Plateau State, amid delays in the arrival of electoral officials and materials in parts of Jos South. As of 4:26 p.m., voters in some wards in Jos South were still waiting for electoral officials and materials, while voting had commenced in parts of Jos East. At Zawan B Ward in Jos South, voting had yet to begin as of 5 p.m., with eligible voters waiting to cast their ballots. “We are ready to participate in the election, but we are still waiting for the electoral officials and materials to arrive,” some voters told our correspondent. In Jos East Local Government Area, however, polling officials arrived around 5 p.m., and voting was underway in Fubor, Shere East and Shere West wards. The Plateau State APC Chairman, Hon. Rufus Bature, said the rerun was being conducted in compliance with a High Court judgment directing the party to hold fresh primaries in the affected wards. “We are addressing you in respect of the court order that was made on APC to have a rerun in eleven wards of Jos South/Jos East Federal Constituency. “As a party which respects court rulings, despite the fact that we are the party in control of government, we have subjected ourselves to that ruling, and today we intend to follow the order of the court,” Bature said. He explained that the exercise, initially scheduled for 8 a.m., was delayed slightly to enable the party to brief the media on developments within the APC in Plateau State. Bature said the electoral and appeal committees were already in place to oversee the process and handle any complaints arising from the exercise. “After the conduct of the elections, if there is any appeal, the committee is already handy to attend to such appeals,” he said. He expressed optimism that the results would be ready by Wednesday evening, describing the exercise as a national assignment. “This is purely a national function. We in the state are just like staff, so I will allow the Chairman of the Electoral Committee and that of the Appeal Committee to address you,” he said. The Chairman of the Electoral Committee and Returning Officer, Hon. Simon Karu Elisha, said the committee was deployed by the party’s national secretariat to conduct the rerun in compliance with the court judgment. “We are here in Plateau State on behalf of the national secretariat of the All Progressives Congress, empowered by the National Chairman, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, in response to the High Court judgment that instructed the APC to conduct a rerun in eleven wards of Jos South/Jos East Federal Constituency,” Karu said. item.title: Moonshot 2026: ‘Your people are your products’ — CEOs share startup growth tips
item.description: By Efosa Taiwo Damilola Olokesusi, chief executive officer of Shuttlers, and Douglas Kendyson, CEO of Selar, have shared insights on financial discipline, hiring, automation and relationship-building as key factors for building and scaling successful businesses. The duo spoke during the “Building Disciplined Businesses That Win” session at the Startup Stage of Moonshot 2026: Courage & Conviction, where they discussed strategies entrepreneurs can adopt to build sustainable businesses and achieve long-term growth. Speaking on the challenges of growing a startup, Olokesusi stressed the importance of regularly reviewing business processes to ensure they remain relevant to changing customer needs and prepare companies for the future. She identified automation as another critical factor, noting that businesses must establish systems to ensure customers receive the services they have been promised. “We have to verify and ensure that things we promised our customers are what they get. E.g having them commute in an AC bus. That’s what we have done to scale our businesses,” she said. On financial discipline, Olokesusi said entrepreneurs must first determine the kind of company they want to build before deciding how to manage their resources. “What type of company are you trying to build before you determine if you are being financially disciplined or you are just saving money,” she said. Explaining Shuttlers’ long-term ambition, she added, “We are trying to be the Dangote of transport.” According to her, financial decisions should reflect a company’s ambitions and the length of time its founders intend to remain in business. Kendyson, meanwhile, encouraged entrepreneurs to identify their priorities and maximise the opportunities that employment and professional relationships can offer, particularly when starting with limited resources. He advised aspiring founders to consider how working for other businesses or gaining employment could help them develop the skills and connections needed to build their own companies. “The best you can do is work as a startup and leverage relationships and you will be very surprised how much that can help you,” he said. Kendyson also highlighted the importance of learning through different career experiences, noting that the relationships and knowledge he gained along his career path had provided leverage for building Selar. Olokesusi further argued that financial discipline must begin with the founder before it can become part of an organisation’s culture. “Your company is a reflection of you as a founder. You need to embody the core value of financial discipline before you can see it in the company,” she said. She also emphasised the importance of recruitment, urging entrepreneurs to be deliberate about the people they bring into their organisations. “People you hire, be particular about that. item.title: ‘We’ll exhume him’ — Toluwanisings’ family rejects cemetery burial
item.description: The family of late Nigerian gospel singer Toluwanisings has threatened to exhume his remains if he is buried in a cemetery rather than beside his late mother at their ancestral home in Oyo State. A representative of the family, in a video circulating on social media, said relatives had agreed that the singer should be brought home and buried at their father’s compound, insisting that they would not accept any alternative arrangement. “We have all decided in the family that Toluwanisings must not be buried in the cemetery. For this reason, they should bring him back home,” the representative said. He warned that the family would take matters into its own hands if the singer were buried in a cemetery. “If you people decide to bury him in the cemetery, we will remove him from there. I am speaking on behalf of all the family members,” he added. The family representative also dismissed concerns about burying the singer at the house he built, insisting that their preferred location was beside his mother’s grave at their father’s compound in Oyo State. “If you say you can’t bury him in his house that he built, we don’t know your reasons and we don’t even care to know, just bring him home,” he said. The dispute has sparked reactions on social media, with some users arguing that the family should have a say in determining the singer’s final resting place. Others have called for a peaceful resolution that respects the deceased and his relatives. Toluwanisings, whose real name was Olayemi Bayonle Bolaji, died on October 14, 2026, at the age of 41. item.title: Usoro warns against fake news, deepfakes ahead of 2027 elections
item.description: FG honours Miden Systems chairman for business integrity By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Federal Government has honoured the Executive Chairman of Miden Systems Limited, Dr Brendan Innocent Usoro, for corporate governance and business integrity, as he warned that fake news and artificial intelligence-generated misinformation posed growing threats to businesses, national security and Nigeria’s 2027 general elections. Usoro received the award at the Nigerian Press Council (NPC) National Summit on Curbing Fake News and Misinformation in the Nigerian Media Space, held in Abuja on Tuesday. The summit, organised under the Federal Ministry of Information and National Orientation, brought together media practitioners, government officials, corporate executives, security agencies and other stakeholders to discuss ways of combating misinformation and promoting responsible journalism. Speaking at the event, Usoro said the growing use of artificial intelligence to generate fake audio recordings, manipulate videos and circulate fabricated reports had made it increasingly difficult for the public to distinguish facts from falsehoods. He said misinformation had extended beyond political campaigns to become a tool for damaging corporate reputations, undermining business confidence and creating social tension. “People use false information to de-market their political opponents, competitors’ products and services, as well as create tension in the polity,” he said. Usoro warned that deepfakes and coordinated disinformation campaigns could manipulate voters, erode public trust and undermine democratic institutions ahead of the 2027 elections. He also disclosed that Miden Systems had experienced what he described as the damaging effects of false information following a financial dispute with a commercial bank. To tackle the problem, he urged Nigerians to verify information before sharing it, recommending independent fact-checking platforms, including Dubawa, to establish the authenticity of reports, photographs and videos. He called for improved training for journalists and fact-checkers, as well as wider access to artificial intelligence-assisted verification tools. Usoro also urged technology companies and regulatory agencies, including the National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA) and the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC), to strengthen collaboration in combating malicious synthetic media. He, however, cautioned that efforts to curb misinformation must not undermine press freedom, freedom of expression or legitimate criticism. On the company’s operations, Usoro said Miden Systems, established in 1997, had expanded from providing safety and equipment maintenance services into a diversified business covering marine services, logistics, offshore and onshore facility upgrades, maintenance and management. item.title: Dickson urges INEC to probe alleged AI-generated voter photos
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — National Leader of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Senator Seriake Dickson, has urged the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to urgently investigate concerns over suspected artificial intelligence-generated photographs and questionable entries in the preliminary voter register published on its website. Dickson described the allegations as a serious matter requiring urgent attention, warning that failure to establish the facts and address any irregularities could undermine public confidence in the 2027 general elections. The former Bayelsa State governor spoke on Wednesday at his Abuja residence when he received the National Coordinator of the Dickson Movement for Democracy, Comrade Ogbidi Emmanuel, and other members of the group, who formally presented the organisation to him and decorated him as its Grand Patron. Dickson said INEC must provide a clear explanation of the allegations and take necessary steps to safeguard the integrity of the voter register. He acknowledged that the commission might have issued a response but maintained that it must go beyond statements to ensure the credibility of the database. “The issue of alleged AI-generated names and photographs in INEC’s voter register is a serious matter that deserves urgent attention. “It is not something that should be dismissed as mere speculation. Concerns have been raised about the authenticity of some entries, and INEC must address them promptly and transparently,” he said. The NDC leader said Nigerians were entitled to assurances that the approximately 103 million registered voters announced by the commission represented genuine and verifiable registrations by eligible citizens. He said the public needed confidence that the register did not contain fictitious identities, fabricated entries or photographs allegedly generated or manipulated using artificial intelligence. “We cannot afford to approach an election as consequential as the 2027 general election with a voter database whose integrity is in doubt,” he said. Dickson added that unreliable voter data could undermine the credibility of the electoral process, stressing the need for the commission to establish the facts surrounding the allegations. He warned that if investigations established that the register contained fictitious identities, photographs of deceased persons or images of individuals who were not eligible Nigerian voters, the development could damage INEC’s credibility and Nigeria’s international standing. He, however, noted that there was still time before the elections for the commission to address the concerns. “I therefore join other concerned Nigerians in calling on INEC to provide a clear explanation, establish the facts and take all necessary measures to clean up the register,” he said. Dickson urged Nigerians to take advantage of the statutory display of the voter register at designated locations to scrutinise entries and report suspicious or inaccurate information

item.title: Osun IPAC disowns members on Adeleke’s PCC list
item.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo The Inter-Party Advisory Council (IPAC) in Osun State has disowned individuals listed as representatives of political parties in the Osun Presidential Campaign Council (PCC) by Governor Ademola Adeleke, the state coordinator of President Bola Tinubu’s campaign council. In a statement issued on Tuesday and endorsed by 11 political parties, Osun IPAC said the individuals listed as its representatives were acting on their own and had not been authorised to represent the council. The parties include Action Alliance, National Rescue Movement, Action Democratic Party, Nigeria Democratic Congress, Social Democratic Party and National Democratic Party. Others are Democratic Leadership Alliance, African Action Congress, Labour Party, Zenith Labour Party and All Progressives Grand Alliance. An advertorial signed by Adeleke and published in a national newspaper had listed Odeleye Titus, Faribido Benson, Enorch Olalekan, Adetunji Olubunmi, Prince Adesoji Adeleke and Rev. Olatunji Popoola as IPAC representatives in the Osun PCC. However, the council said the inclusion of their names was misleading and could create confusion over its representation. “We wish to state categorically and for the record, that the persons whose names were paraded as IPAC members in the said council are not our representatives, nor were they, at any point in time, nominated or authorised by the council to represent us in any capacity,” the statement said. IPAC described itself as a structured body with recognised leadership and member political parties, insisting that any representation must follow due process and official communication from its secretariat. The council said it completely dissociated itself from the list, warning against using its name to score political points or create a false impression of broad-based acceptance. It also urged President Tinubu not to recognise the individuals listed as its representatives in the Osun PCC, insisting that its legitimate stakeholders were parties with strong grassroots presence across the state’s local government areas. “We are the majority members of IPAC in Osun State with strong grassroots presence across all local governments, and any engagement with IPAC in the state should be through us,” the statement added. The post Osun IPAC disowns members on Adeleke’s PCC list appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Oborevwori signs five bills into law in Delta
item.description: By Egufe Yafugborhi and Ochuko Akuopha ASABA — Delta State Governor, Sheriff Oborevwori, has signed five bills into law, saying the measures are aimed at strengthening public institutions, improving service delivery and securing a better future for residents. Oborevwori assented to the bills at Government House, Asaba, on Wednesday, describing them as part of his administration’s reform efforts under the MORE Agenda. “I assented to five bills, three amendments, one consolidated, and a brand-new one passed by the Delta State House of Assembly,” the governor said. The new laws are the Delta State Revenue Service (Consolidated) Law, 2026; Delta State Public and Private Properties Protection (Amendment) Law, 2026; High Court (Amendment) Law, 2026; Customary Court of Appeal (Amendment) Law, 2026; and Payment of Thirteenth Month Salary Law, 2026. Oborevwori said the laws would strengthen accountability, protect public assets, reinforce the rule of law and improve workers’ morale. “Together, we have strengthened accountability, safeguarded public assets, reinforced the rule of law and boosted public servants’ morale,” he said. He added that the measures reflected his administration’s determination to build institutions that serve residents with fairness, efficiency and respect. “These efforts reflect our resolve to build institutions that serve our people with fairness, efficiency and respect, while securing a better future for our people,” he said. The governor stressed that development went beyond infrastructure to include policies capable of improving people’s lives. On the Thirteenth Month Salary Law, Oborevwori said the initiative was intended to boost workers’ morale, reward their contributions and improve productivity. He also said the amendments to the laws governing the judiciary would increase the number of High Court judges from 46 to 50 and Customary Court of Appeal judges from nine to 12, with a view to improving justice delivery. According to him, the laws would strengthen public institutions, improve service delivery and promote economic development. Presenting the bills, Speaker of the Delta State House of Assembly, Rt. Hon. Emomotimi Guwor, said the measures would strengthen governance, improve justice delivery and protect investments. The post Oborevwori signs five bills into law in Delta appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: [UPDATED] High-Speed Train Collision In Spain Kills 64, Injures Over 100
item.description: A high-speed train collision south of Madrid in Spain killed 64 people and injured scores more on Wednesday, with the toll likely to rise, authorities said in one of Europe’s deadliest such disasters this century. One train on the scene in the central region of Castilla-La Mancha was seen embedded into another after the second such accident to strike Spain this year. This still image from video taken and released by Spain’s Civil Guard on October 28, 2026 shows an aerial scene of a train crash between a high-speed Renfe AVE train and an Iryo train around 150 km south of Madrid between Urda and Los Yebenes in the province of Toledo. (Photo by Handout / Guardia Civil / AFP) Some carriages were lying on their side in tangles of metal debris at the bottom of an embankment, while dozens of emergency services vehicles were racing to and from the site. “We are speaking of approximately 64 (dead), but this is probably going to grow even more,” Castilla-La Mancha’s leader Emiliano Garcia-Page told reporters at the scene, raising a previous toll of 31. A spokeswoman from the Castilla-La Mancha government said that more than 100 people had been injured. Of them, 58 had been taken to hospital, with 15 in a critical condition. Helicopters hovered above the site during a frantic search for survivors, while several black vans arrived from a funeral parlour. State railway operator Renfe confirmed in a statement that the main high-speed line from Madrid to southern Spain had been suspended after one of its services suffered an accident with a train from private Spanish company Iryo. Iryo said in a statement that its train, which was carrying 147 passengers and five staff, including the driver, “was hit from behind” by the Renfe service. This still image from video taken and released by Spain’s Emergency Military Unit (UME) on October 28, 2026 shows military rescue personnel working at the scene of a train crash between a high-speed Renfe AVE train and an Iryo train around 150 km south of Madrid between Urda and Los Yebenes in the province of Toledo. Photo by HANDOUT / UME / AFP A visibly shaken Manuel Ortiz, 49, who lives in the nearby village of Urda, around 130 kilometres (80 miles) south of Madrid, told AFP he had been transporting survivors all morning in his car. Ortiz added that the passengers of the Iryo told him their train was stationary when the collision happened, describing a “horrific, horrible” scene that “smelled of an accident, of metal”. Rail Safety Under Scrutiny The accident comes one month before Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez, who faced heavy criticism for this year’s first disaster, seeks to overturn unfavourable polls and extend his eight-year premiership in an early general election on November 29. Sanchez’s office said he was heading to the scene. The premier had said on X that he was “shocked” by the accident and sent “my love, solidarity and support to all the victims and their families”.
